choices.text: Agree - doubling the radius doubles the area
Disagree - the area has quadrupled, from 25 pi to 100 pi
Disagree - the area stays the same

questions.feedback: That doubled-area answer is the one to unlearn: Doubling the radius doubles the area of a circle. Reteach point: Area scales with the square of the radius: double the radius and the area quadruples.
questions.misconception: Doubling the radius doubles the area of a circle.
questions.prompt: A circle of radius 5 cm is enlarged to radius 10 cm. A classmate says its area has doubled. Which response is correct?

questions.feedback: Scene s1 fixes this: a semicircle is half the circumference, 1/2 x 2 pi x 10 = 10 pi cm.
questions.prompt: State the arc length of a semicircle of radius 10 cm, in terms of pi.

questions.feedback: Scene s2: pyramid volume is 1/3 x base area x height = 1/3 x 30 x 9 = 90 cubic centimetres.
questions.prompt: A pyramid has base area 30 square centimetres and vertical height 9 cm. What is its volume?

questions.feedback: Scene s3: volume is 4/3 pi r cubed = 4/3 x pi x 216 = 288 pi cubic centimetres.
questions.prompt: A sphere has radius 6 cm. Write its volume in terms of pi.
